topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school or undergraduate students with an interest in physics and mathematics

outline.topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi
outline.target_audience: High school or undergraduate students with an interest in physics and mathematics

sections.title: The Setup: The Two-Block System
sections.content: Introduce a 1D frictionless track with two blocks of different masses, m1 and m2, and a wall. The smaller block is between the larger block and the wall. We model the elastic collisions between them.
sections.example: A small hamster (m=1kg) and a large elephant (m=100kg). The hamster is sandwiched between the elephant and a vertical cliff face.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly review the laws of Conservation of Momentum and Kinetic Energy. Explain that for perfectly elastic collisions, these laws allow us to derive a 'transition rule' for the velocity vectors of the two objects.
sections.example: Visualizing the collision as a vector transformation: The velocities of the blocks jump to new states dictated by their mass ratio after each impact.

sections.title: Visualizing the Phase Space
sections.content: Introduce the 'Phase Space' diagram. Instead of tracking positions, we plot the velocity of Block 1 vs. Block 2. Each collision represents a reflection across a line in this 2D plane.
sections.example: An animation showing a particle bouncing inside a circular sector (a 'wedge') in the velocity plane. The angle of the wedge is determined by the ratio of the masses.

sections.title: The Magic Link: Emergence of Pi
sections.content: As the mass ratio m2/m1 approaches 100^n, the number of collisions matches the first n digits of pi. Explain that the geometric reflection angle in phase space is related to the trigonometric expansion of pi.
sections.example: A digital counter on screen: When the elephant is 100 times heavier than the hamster, we get 3 collisions. At 10,000 times, we get 31, and at 1,000,000 times, we get 314.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition
sections.content: Conclude that the conservation of energy creates a circular constraint in the phase space. The discrete counting of collisions is simply measuring the 'arc' of this circle, essentially computing the circumference/diameter ratio.
sections.example: A final visual overlay: The path of the blocks in velocity space perfectly tracing the curve of a circle, illustrating why pi naturally appears in the count.

storyboard.title: The Setup: The Two-Block System
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless track.
A wall forces the smaller block to rebound.
Massive blocks create extreme velocity differences.
animations: Create two blocks, #FF0000 and #00FF00, at horizontal positions.
Animate blocks colliding, changing #FF0000 color to #FFFFFF.
Show reflection of #FF0000 block against a wall, #0000FF.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Energy and momentum remain constant throughout collisions.
These laws dictate post-collision velocity changes.
Collisions act as transformations of velocity vectors.
animations: Visualize energy circle #FFFF00 representing total kinetic energy.
Show block momentum vectors as arrows, #FF8000.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Phase Space
lecture_lines: Map block velocities as coordinates in a plane.
Each collision is a reflection in phase space.
The trajectory bounces within a geometric wedge.
animations: Draw phase space grid, #404040, for block velocities.
Plot trajectory of collision events in phase space, #FF00FF.
Highlight geometric shape of trajectory, #00FFFF, indicating Pi.

storyboard.title: The Magic Link: Emergence of Pi
lecture_lines: Bigger mass ratios mean more total collisions.
Number of collisions matches digits of Pi.
Mass ratios encode decimal expansions of Pi.
Reflection angles define the arc of the circle.
Geometric constraints link physics to circle math.
animations: Rotate phase space trajectory to show symmetry, #FFCC00.
Overlay circular arc, #00FF00, tracing the trajectory path.
Animate circle subdivision to reveal Pi digit count, #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Summary and Intuition
lecture_lines: Phase space paths trace a circular arc.
Counting collisions measures the arc's length.
Physics naturally emerges from the geometry of Pi.
animations: Summarize collision events as a series of reflections, #FF0000.
Animate total reflections converging to value of Pi, #00FF00.
Fade out all elements leaving only the Pi symbol, #FFFFFF.
